food_name: Common mugwort (Artemisia vulgaris), dried aerial parts
food_part: Aerial parts (composite above-ground material; culinary species, edible leaves documented)
mapping_review_rationale: Primary LC-MS study used eupatorin standard and reports 0.97 µg/g dry weight plant material for authenticated A. vulgaris; this culinary herb species has documented edible leaf use. Retain the study’s aerial-parts matrix and dry basis explicitly.
analytical_method: LC-MS/MS in MRM mode; retention time and mass spectra compared with standards
extraction_method: 10 g dried plant material extracted three times with 200 mL methanol for 1 h at room temperature; extract diluted for HPLC
sample_size: Not stated in Table 2; do not assign a sample count
source_title: HPLC analysis of phenolic compounds from Artemisia species
database_reference: Table 2; A. vulgaris; eupatorin concentration 0.97 µg/g dry weight plant material
extraction_notes: The measured matrix is dried, authenticated A. vulgaris aerial parts, not a prepared dish or infusion. Culinary use evidence is separate: Kew Plants of the World Online classifies A. vulgaris as used for food; leaves are used as a culinary herb. Do not infer an intake concentration for an unspecified serving or leaf-only portion.
uncertainty_notes: Table 2 gives 0.97 µg/g dry plant material for A. vulgaris. The paper describes the species as medicinal plants and analyzes aerial parts as a composite matrix. Food-use eligibility relies on independent documented culinary use of the species/leaves; species-level, dry aerial-part concentration retained without fresh-weight conversion.
